messages:
Priya Rao: Quick sync: product asked to prioritize a safer rollout path for kernel pluggability + a stricter KV retention default. I put a short spec in the PRD draft; want feedback on scope and gating.
Ethan Brooks: Can you paste the key launch gates here? makes it easier to comment.
Priya Rao: Yep, pasted gist: 
``nLAUNCH GATES (proposal):
- Perf: P95 latency no worse than +8% vs baseline across short/med/long seq buckets (8, 128, 1024).
- Correctness: generation QA delta < 1.5% on our core eval set; rerun with quantized kernels.
- Safety: per-tenant KV namespaces default ON; any cross-tenant key access must be impossible.
- Observability: audit events emitted on kernel switch + route-level metric for kernel mix.
- Rollout: canary progression 0.5% -> 3% -> 15% -> 100% with 12h soak at 15%.
- Rollback: automated if error rate >3x baseline or SLO violations for 10m.
``n(Note: dedicated customers can opt-in to faster progression after SOC sign-off)
Marta Gomez: For the seq buckets, 1024 might blow up KV; we need an eviction backstop for >2048 tokens. Add that as an edge case.
Leo Hart: Agreed. Also we should require a fallback kernel that is compatible with custom CUDA ops (many enterprise models use custom ops). Add a compatibility matrix test as a pre-launch step.
Rina Sato: Ops ask: add a "trace-id" correlation on kernel selection events so we can correlate latency with model inputs. Without that, debugging tail latency will be rough.
Priya Rao: Good catch. Add to observability gate: kernel_selection.trace_id and kernel_selection.reasons.
Ethan Brooks: How are we defining baseline? current prod runtime on prod-cluster-1 during 10th-16th last month? we need reproducible baseline harness.
Priya Rao: Baseline = prod runtime snapshot from last stable deploy (prod-2026-02-08) using our canned perf scenarios. We'll publish run scripts in the PRD.
Marta Gomez: Customer ask: AtlasCorp wants predictability for long-context chats; they want a hard cap on KV eviction for pinned sessions. Can we make per-route KV retention tunable but default conservative?
Leo Hart: Implementation note: per-route retention tunable is fine but must be rate-limited to avoid memory exhaustion. Default conservative value: 30m TTL + LRU eviction with per-tenant memory budget.
Rina Sato: Security: if we namespace keys per-tenant we must also rotate namespace keys on tenant removal. Add lifecycle policy to PRD.
InfraBot: checkpoint: canary-plan: created id=cp-2362001234, clusters=[us-east-1-canary, eu-west-1-canary], target=0.5%
Priya Rao: Tradeoff discussion: do we ship kernel pluggability and tighter KV defaults as a single change or split into two rollouts? My instinct: split. Kernel selector touches execution path and perf; KV default is a config change and should be lower-risk to ship first. Thoughts?
Ethan Brooks: +1 split. Roll KV defaults as a config toggle immediately (with tenant opt-out), then follow with kernel selector after we prove lower tail latency.
Marta Gomez: Splitting also helps with release timelines  we can get KV changes out in 2 sprints and kernel selector in 4.
Leo Hart: If we split, still run an integration test where both are active to ensure no unexpected interactions. Add an integration job to CI that runs the selector + KV retention on smaller infra.
Priya Rao: OK action items: 
- Priya: update PRD to split the initiatives and add the observability bits + baseline definition.
- Ethan: draft the KV rollout playbook (tenant opt-out flow, memory guardrails).
- Marta: add compatibility matrix and long-seq eviction backstop tests.
- Leo: CI integration job + fallback kernel doc.
- Rina: security lifecycle for tenant namespace keys.
All: async review on GH PR by Friday EOD. We'll do RFC review next Tue 9:30.
Ethan Brooks: tiny nit: lower the canary soak at 15% to 12h -> maybe 24h? ops prefers 24h for long-tail metrics.
Priya Rao: Let's keep 12h for initial plan but call out a 24h recommended soak for high-risk customers or models with known tail issues.
Marta Gomez: Done. I'm +1 to split and ship KV defaults first.
Rina Sato: +1
Leo Hart: +1
Priya Rao: Thanks team. I'll link PRD here when updated.
